text:
The Sharks are 10-11-2, and for the first time in a while the record isn't the point. Macklin Celebrini, Will Smith and now Ivar Stenberg, this summer's second overall pick, are the most talked-about trio in San Jose, and Sunday's 4-2 win that ended Nashville's seven-game streak showed why: the three of them combined for three goals and passing that had the beat writers gasping. With Igor Chernyshov instead of Stenberg, the Smith and Celebrini line has taken 62% of the expected goals (the quality of chances).

The rest of the roster is the honest part. San Jose has 43.5% of the expected goals overall and 45% at five on five, and the penalty kill gives up a full expected goal a game. Both top pairings, Darnell Nurse with Michael Kesselring and Jacob Trouba with Sam Dickinson, are under 45% of the chances, and Nurse's pair has been outscored 13-6. Goaltending has saved the Sharks almost 12 goals beyond expected, with Yaroslav Askarov's start drawing a lot of attention and Alex Nedeljkovic stealing Sunday.

Dmitry Orlov is running hot, 9 points in 10. Kiefer Sherwood left Sunday's game with no update, and Smith took his place on the top power play. Our simulations give San Jose a 9% playoff chance and about 78 points. For this season, the kids' development is the story worth following, and it's a good one.
